# Crease patterns vs. the Swiss roll {#comparison}

*Does the new benchmark actually add anything?*

<!-- TODO: chapter content. Outline below is the plan of record. -->

- Head-to-head against Swiss roll and S-curve, same methods and same metrics.
- What separates the benchmarks is the SPREAD between methods at matched
  difficulty, not a flip in their order. E1 looked for a flip and found none; it
  found a separation, with an interval from a cluster bootstrap over settings and
  a p-value from cluster-robust regression. A benchmark earns its keep by telling
  methods apart, and that is the statistic the chapter reports -- read from
  `e1-controlled.rds` through an inline `r` expression, ratio and interval
  together, never the ratio alone.
- What the crease-pattern family surfaces that a single fixed geometry hides.
- An honest answer to "why not just use the Swiss roll?"
